knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Tying the reward to a completed paid job keeps the cost linked to revenue. Paying on a mention or before any job creates an open-ended cost.
Commercial electronic messages need consent and a valid sender, and the rules should be checked before sending. Sending to a purchased or unconsented list is the error the lesson warns about.
A cap limits the total reward per referrer in a set period, which makes the cost predictable. It must be stated in the written terms.

practicalCriteria: The learner writes a one-page referral terms sheet that contains a reward, a trigger, a cap and an end date, and the assessor confirms that all four are present and that the trigger is a completed paid event.
The learner marks each consumer and messaging point as confirmed, and the assessor confirms that no point is marked confirmed without a source and date.
From a supplied referral log, the learner calculates the cost per referred paying customer, and the assessor checks the figure against the log.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off stays separate. A quiz pass is not verified practical competence.
evidenceRequired: Signed-off referral terms sheet with date
Referral log with first paid jobs and rewards paid
stopWorkCriteria: Stop sending any referral message to a contact who has not consented.
Stop any reward scheme whose terms are not in writing.
